chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Ali from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed li'an with his wife while she was pregnant, and her pregnancy had become evident, and he denied what was in her womb. When she gave birth to it, he claimed it and acknowledged it, and asserted that it was from him. He said: 'The child is returned to him, and he inherits it, and he is not lashed, because the li'an between them has passed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an when the wife is pregnant and the husband later acknowledges the child?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the finality of the li'an process precludes the husband from being flogged again, even if he later acknowledges the child after its birth. This ruling underscores the principle that li'an serves as a definitive severance of the marital bond and attribution of lineage, rendering the child legitimate to the husband for inheritance purposes without the penalty of *hudud* for false accusation.
